summary: A hostile wood nymph steals the hero's wielded cockatrice corpse at step 229. At step 230 C enters trap.c:minstapetrify through steal.c:steal after the nymph fails its glove check, then displays the slowing-down effect; JS records the stale note_unported('mon.c minstapetrify') and returns -1 without applying the helper. This is the same missing trap.c:minstapetrify implementation as the grouped ogre case, reached through a different production caller.

source.branch: In steal.c:steal, a stolen cockatrice corpse with no gloves calls minstapetrify(mtmp, TRUE). The helper performs the same stone-resistance and vampire/form checks as the grouped hero-cockatrice ogre case, then lowers monster speed, displays its transformation when visible, and credits the hero with xkilled. The recorded nymph reaches the speed/message branch.
callers: trap.c:minstapetrify shared with the grouped v51 cockatrice-versus-ogre case via uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_ston

evidence: The admitted v51 baseline matches through segment 0 step 229. At step 230 C's first changed screen shows the nymph's slowing-down effect and the cursor moves to [71,0,1]; JS still shows the nymph at [76,0,1]. The first RNG difference is at step 231, after the helper should have run.

The admitted recipe source pointer is steal.c:steal -> trap.c:minstapetrify(mtmp, TRUE). nethack-c/upstream/src/steal.c:343-617 contains the corpse theft branch at line 610; nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:3858-3882 defines the missing helper.
js/steal.js:846 currently records note_unported('mon.c minstapetrify') after mpickobj and preserves steal's -1 result. The marker names the wrong C owner: the call resolves to trap.c:minstapetrify.

This admitted case and v51-cockatrice-levitation-ogre-action-attempt2 both fail because the same trap.c function is absent. The cases exercise separate active callers (steal.c:steal and uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_ston), so they are grouped in one helper port rather than counted as separate implementation tasks.
